supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Lively Hawaiian set shines on Easy Wind and New Speedway despite muddy matrix mix
ai_show_review.blurb: The band delivers strong performances of Easy Wind, Good Lovin' and a rousing New Speedway Boogie. Recording quality is uneven, with crystal‑clear soundboard sections offset by muddy audience portions.
ai_show_review.review: On June 13, 1970 the Dead turned the Honolulu Civic Auditorium into a breezy tropical playground. The first half of the set rolls from an upbeat Cold Rain And Snow straight into a scorching Easy Wind where Phil’s bass is front‑and‑center, and Jerry’s guitar, though often buried in the matrix mix, erupts with hot licks when it cuts through. Good Lovin' gets two treatments – the first segues into a drum break before returning for a second round that lets Bob push his rhythm forward. The centerpiece of the night is New Speedway Boogie; a guest keyboard adds sparkle and the band rides a tight groove that feels locked in despite the uneven audio. The show closes on a high note with a fiery Turn On Your Lovelight* that captures the energy of a Hawaiian vacation, even if the mix occasionally drops into ‘dank’ snare buzz. Overall, the performance is vibrant and full‑of‑joy, though listeners will have to navigate a patchwork of crystal‑clear SBD moments and muddy audience bleed.

best_recording.reason: Only available source; despite fair‑to‑poor matrix quality it contains the clearest soundboard sections of the performance.

key_highlights: Phil’s bass drives an electrifying Easy Wind that stands out even in a mixed mix.
New Speedway Boogie shines with guest keyboards and tight band chemistry.
Two Good Lovin' renditions bookend the set, giving Bob extra presence in the mix.
Turn On Your Lovelight* closes the night with high energy despite occasional snare buzz.

band_performance.Jerry: Often buried in the mix but when audible his playing is hot, especially on Easy Wind.
band_performance.Phil: Bass drives Easy Wind hard and provides a solid foundation throughout the set.
band_performance.Bob: Pushed forward at times, leading several jams and adding noticeable presence.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are razor‑sharp yet sometimes sit in the background with snare buzz due to mix issues.
band_performance.Billy: Shares the crisp rhythmic drive with Mickey, though both can be masked by the uneven matrix sound.
